Main contributions include: (i) high-accuracy moment estimation and CCDF characterization via WCE minimizing Monte Carlo variance; (ii) Markovian projection reducing infinite-dimensional dynamics to tractable systems ([MATH]) for Rayleigh, Rician, and Nakagami models under stated assumptions; (iii) asymptotically optimal importance sampling weights derived from Malliavin sensitivities, achieving 839 to 2516x variance reductions; (iv) a theoretically grounded and provably efficient adaptive SGD algorithm with Robbins-Monro step size schedule for parameter estimation. Numerical experiments validate our approach with relative errors below 0.5\%, enabling gradient-based optimization of fade duration statistics even for regimes where [MATH], without requiring [MATH] samples, by evaluating sensitivities through analytical Malliavin weights.
tldr: This paper applies Wiener Chaos Expansion and Malliavin Calculus to analyze fade duration in wireless channels, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: Fade duration analysis is important for wireless communication, but the paper focuses on classical stochastic methods and does not involve quantum systems or information theory.
method: The authors use Wiener Chaos Expansion, Malliavin Calculus, and importance sampling with adaptive SGD to estimate fade duration statistics.
result: The method achieves high accuracy and significant variance reduction (up to 2516x) for rare-event probability estimation.
conclusion: The proposed framework is effective for classical wireless channel modeling but has no relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Joint Chance Constrained Safe-Optimal Control
authors: Niklas Schmid, Jared Miller, Tristan Zeller, Marta Fochesato, Tobias Sutter, John Lygeros
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the finite-time optimal control of stochastic systems subject to a probabilistic constraint on the trajectories' safety. Such formulations are known as joint chance constrained optimal control problems. The common practice is to jointly minimise the expected cost of all trajectories, safe and unsafe. This leads to policies which invite constraint violations to exploit low-cost unsafe trajectories. When constraints represent states of critical failure, such behaviour is undesirable. We demonstrate that this behaviour can be overcome by only minimizing the expected cost of safe trajectories. The underlying rationale follows a practical intuition: In many applications, the cost incurred by unsafe trajectories is irrelevant (e.g., the battery usage of a crashed quadcopter), and one is usually interested in minimizing the cost of trajectories that are safe. We show that this problem can be cast as a constrained Markov Decision Process over an augmented state space. This allows solving it via dynamic programming. We derive bounds on the policies' safety under errors resulting from gridding approximations when the system's state space is continuous. Finally, we empirically compare dynamic programming as well as reinforcement learning solutions on a simulated 2D unicycle system in cluttered reach-avoid environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a safe-optimal control framework for stochastic systems with joint chance constraints, minimizing expected cost only over safe trajectories.
motivation: Standard joint chance-constrained optimal control minimizes expected cost over all trajectories, which can lead to policies that exploit low-cost unsafe trajectories. The authors aim to avoid this by focusing on safe trajectories only.
method: The problem is formulated as a constrained Markov Decision Process over an augmented state space and solved via dynamic programming. Bounds on safety under grid approximation errors are derived, and reinforcement learning solutions are compared.
result: The approach yields policies that avoid unsafe trajectories even when they are low-cost, and dynamic programming solutions are validated on a simulated 2D unicycle system.
conclusion: Minimizing cost only over safe trajectories is a viable alternative to standard joint chance-constrained control, producing safer policies without sacrificing performance on safe trajectories.

title: Nekhoroshev Theorem For Time Quasiperiodic Perturbations Of P-Steep Systems
authors: Dario Bambusi, Santiago Barbieri, Mar Giralt, Beatrice Langella
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Nekhoroshev type result for a time quasiperiodic perturbation of an integrable Hamiltonian system. More precisely, we assume that the integrable part is analytic and fulfills a generic nondegeneracy condition introduced by Nekhoroshev and called P-Steepness. We add a small perturbation which depends in a quasiperiodic way on time (with Diophantine frequency) and prove that -- for times exponentially long with the inverse of the size [MATH] of the perturbation -- the actions of the unperturbed system remain approximately constant. The proof is based on an extension to the time dependent case of the proof {of classical Nekhoroshev's theorem} given by Guzzo, Chierchia and Benettin, which however requires new ideas in order to deal with the more complex geometry of resonances of the time dependent case.
tldr: This paper proves a Nekhoroshev theorem for time quasiperiodic perturbations of integrable Hamiltonian systems, ensuring long-term stability of actions.
motivation: To extend classical Nekhoroshev theory to time-dependent perturbations, which is important for understanding stability in non-autonomous Hamiltonian systems.
method: The proof extends the approach of Guzzo, Chierchia, and Benettin to the time-dependent case, handling the more complex resonance geometry.
result: For exponentially long times (in the inverse perturbation size), the actions remain approximately constant under a small quasiperiodic perturbation with Diophantine frequency.
conclusion: The result provides a rigorous stability estimate for a broad class of time-dependent Hamiltonian systems, generalizing the classical Nekhoroshev theorem.

title: $\texttt{bucket-graph-spprc}$: An Extensible C++ Library For The Shortest Path Problem With Resource Constraints
authors: Simon Spoorendonk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present [MATH] ([MATH] for short), an open-source, header-only C++23 library for the shortest path problem with resource constraints (SPPRC), the pricing subproblem at the heart of branch-cut-and-price for vehicle routing and related problems. The library implements the bucket-graph labelling algorithm of Sadykov, Uchoa and Pessoa (2021), with bidirectional labelling, across-arc concatenation, bucket fixing and arc elimination, and a structure-of-arrays label store with SIMD-accelerated dominance. Its central design feature is a compile-time resource concept: a new SPPRC variant is added by implementing a fixed seven-function interface, and resources compose into a label state with no runtime dispatch, the state layout fixed at compile time. Five resources ship built in: time/capacity, ng-path elementarity relaxation, rank-1 cuts, cumulative cost, and pickup-and-delivery. In a reproducible, head-to-head comparison on shared public instances at an identical bound, [MATH] outperforms PathWyse (Salani, Basso and Giuffrida, 2024), the main open-source comparator, by [MATH]--[MATH] in shifted geometric mean (and by [MATH]--[MATH] even when itself run single-threaded), and runs within [MATH]--[MATH] of parallel pull labelling (Petersen and Spoorendonk, 2025), a different labelling technique for the same problem. The library, benchmark scripts, and pinned instances are publicly available.
tldr: This paper presents an optimized C++ library for the shortest path problem with resource constraints, a combinatorial optimization problem used in vehicle routing.
motivation: Efficiently solving the pricing subproblem in branch-cut-and-price algorithms for vehicle routing and related problems.
method: Implements the bucket-graph labelling algorithm with bidirectional labelling, SIMD-accelerated dominance, and a compile-time resource concept for extensibility.
result: Outperforms the main open-source comparator PathWyse by 2.5–3.5× in shifted geometric mean, and runs within 1.2–1.5× of a parallel pull labelling baseline.
conclusion: The library provides a fast, extensible, and reproducible implementation for SPPRC, advancing practical optimization but not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Analysis Of Gradual Changes In Nonparametric Regression Based On A New Optimization Method In The Non-unique Case
authors: Marie Hu\v{s}kov\'a, Natalie Neumeyer, Leonie Selk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a nonparametric regression model with one-dimensional covariates and a continuous regression function. Assume that the regression function from the left of the covariate support starts equal to zero and then changes at some unknown point. Our aim is to estimate this gradual change point. We define and compare various consistent estimators based on a new general optimization method in the case where the aim is to estimate the largest minimization point of some objective function. We discuss rates of convergence and estimating the regression function based on the gradual change structure. Bootstrap bias approximation is discussed. Further applications in a two sample case are considered, where two continuous regression functions first equal and then change at some point of interest.
tldr: This paper proposes a new optimization method to estimate gradual change points in nonparametric regression, with applications in two-sample comparisons.
motivation: Estimating change points in regression functions is important in many fields, but existing methods often assume unique minimizers; this work addresses the non-unique case.
method: The authors define consistent estimators based on a new general optimization method that finds the largest minimization point of an objective function, and discuss rates of convergence and bootstrap bias approximation.
result: The estimators are shown to be consistent, and the method is extended to two-sample problems where two regression functions are initially equal and then diverge.
conclusion: The proposed optimization method provides a way to estimate gradual changes in nonparametric regression even when the objective function has multiple minimizers.

title: Coarse Embeddability Ratios Of Banach Spaces
authors: Avik Das
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given two Banach spaces [MATH] and [MATH], one can associate a numerical invariant [MATH], called the coarse embeddability ratio, which provides a criterion for coarse and uniform embeddability. We compute the coarse embeddability ratio for several important classes of Banach spaces, using various tools from the nonlinear theory of Banach spaces. Finally, we find pairs of Banach spaces with arbitrarily large coarse embeddability ratio, resolving an open problem of Rosendal in the negative.
tldr: This paper studies coarse embeddability ratios of Banach spaces, a topic in functional analysis with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to compute coarse embeddability ratios for various Banach spaces and resolve an open problem by Rosendal.
method: The author uses tools from the nonlinear theory of Banach spaces to compute the invariant for several classes of spaces.
result: The paper finds pairs of Banach spaces with arbitrarily large coarse embeddability ratio, answering Rosendal's question in the negative.
conclusion: The work contributes to the geometry of Banach spaces but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Fuel-Optimal Low-Thrust Trajectory Design Under High-Fidelity Dynamics: A State Transition Matrix-Based Sensitivity Approach
authors: Liqiang Hou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A straightforward and computationally efficient indirect method based on STM sensitivity analysis is introduced for designing fuel-optimal low-thrust transfers under high-fidelity dynamics. Conventional indirect approaches require explicit expressions for the partial derivatives of the system dynamics to formulate the costate equations, making the derivation process complex for high-fidelity trajectory design. In this work, the costate equations are reformulated as ordinary differential equations involving only the state variables and their time derivatives. High-order dynamical effects are treated as black-box components, avoiding the need to derive partial derivatives of the system dynamics. A standard gradient-based or interior-point optimizer is used to determine the optimal costates and transfer parameters. The equivalence between the proposed method and conventional approaches is demonstrated through a classic Earth-Mars transfer scenario. An Earth-Mars transfer under high-fidelity dynamics is then presented, including perturbations from solar radiation pressure, solar J2 oblateness, Jupiter third-body gravity, and relativistic effects. Finally, the method is applied to a multiple-revolution Earth-Venus transfer under high-fidelity dynamics.
tldr: This paper presents a fuel-optimal low-thrust trajectory design method using state transition matrix sensitivity analysis for high-fidelity dynamics.
motivation: Conventional indirect methods for fuel-optimal trajectory design require complex derivation of partial derivatives for high-fidelity dynamics, which is cumbersome.
method: The costate equations are reformulated using only state variables and their time derivatives, treating high-order dynamics as black-box components, and solved with a standard optimizer.
result: The method is validated on Earth-Mars and Earth-Venus transfers under high-fidelity perturbations including solar radiation pressure, J2 oblateness, third-body gravity, and relativistic effects.
conclusion: The proposed approach simplifies the derivation process and is computationally efficient for high-fidelity trajectory design.

title: Chaos On Surfaces And Beyond: A New Notion Of Dynamical Hyperbolicity
authors: J\'er\^ome Buzzi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present some developments in the study of chaotic dynamics following the solution of a conjecture of Newhouse on the measures maximizing the entropy of smooth surface diffeomorphisms. We focus on , a generalization of the classical Anosov-Smale theory of uniform hyperbolicity introduced in a joint work with Sylvain Crovisier and Omri Sarig. This new property is general enough to be satisfied by all smooth surface diffeomorphisms with positive entropy, yet it still ensures many quantitative properties such as exponential mixing or limit theorems for regular functions. We also present some open problems, including its abundance (or not) in higher dimensions.
tldr: This paper presents a new notion of dynamical hyperbolicity for smooth surface diffeomorphisms with positive entropy, generalizing uniform hyperbolicity.
motivation: To understand chaotic dynamics and prove quantitative properties like exponential mixing for a broad class of systems beyond uniform hyperbolicity.
method: Introduces a new property called 'chaos on surfaces' and proves it holds for all smooth surface diffeomorphisms with positive entropy, using techniques from smooth dynamics and ergodic theory.
result: The new hyperbolicity notion ensures exponential mixing and limit theorems for regular functions, and the paper discusses open problems including its extension to higher dimensions.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for chaotic dynamics on surfaces, but its relevance to quantum information theory or information thermodynamics is negligible.

title: Surjective Isometries On The Positive Parts Of The Unit Spheres Of Some Function Spaces
authors: Yuta Enami, Daisuke Hirota, Hironao Koshimizu, Min-Ruei Lin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the space [MATH] of continuously differentiable functions on the closed unit interval [MATH] and the space [MATH] of Lipschitz continuous functions on [MATH], equipped with the norms \|f\|_{\sigma, p} = \sqrt[p]{|f(0)|^p + \|f'\|_\infty^p} & (1 \le p < \infty), \\ \max\{\, |f(0)|, \|f'\|_\infty \,\} & (p = \infty). We show that every surjective isometry on the positive part of the unit sphere extends to a surjective complex-linear isometry on the entire space. As a corollary, every such isometry also extends to an isometric order isomorphism on the real subspaces [MATH] and [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies surjective isometries on the positive part of the unit sphere of certain function spaces, specifically spaces of continuously differentiable and Lipschitz functions with a specific norm.
motivation: To understand the structure of isometries on function spaces, particularly how isometries on the positive part of the unit sphere extend to the whole space.
method: The authors consider the spaces C^1[0,1] and Lip[0,1] equipped with a norm combining the function value at 0 and the sup norm of the derivative. They prove that every surjective isometry on the positive part of the unit sphere extends to a surjective complex-linear isometry on the entire space.
result: Every surjective isometry on the positive part of the unit sphere extends to a surjective complex-linear isometry on the whole space, and also extends to an isometric order isomorphism on the real subspaces.
conclusion: The result provides a characterization of isometries on these function spaces, showing that isometries on the positive part determine the full isometry group.

title: Fractional Integral And Fractional Maximal Operators On Generalized Fofana Spaces
authors: Pokou Nagacy, B\'erenger Akon Kpata, Nouffou Diarra
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalized Fofana spaces were recently introduced as generalizations of Fofana spaces and Nakai's generalized Morrey spaces. In this paper, we establish the boundedness properties of the following operators in these spaces: fractional integral operators, fractional maximal operators and generalized fractional integral operators. As a consequence, we obtain generalized Olsen-type inequalities involving the Riesz potential and generalized fractional integral operators.
tldr: This paper studies boundedness of fractional integral and maximal operators on generalized Fofana spaces, which are function spaces unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: To extend known boundedness results for fractional operators to a new class of function spaces.
method: The authors prove boundedness properties using techniques from harmonic analysis and function space theory.
result: They establish boundedness of fractional integral, fractional maximal, and generalized fractional integral operators on generalized Fofana spaces, and derive Olsen-type inequalities.
conclusion: The results contribute to the theory of function spaces and harmonic analysis, but have no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Difference-of-Convex Optimization Via Inexact Smoothing Descent Methods: Difference Of High-Order Moreau Envelopes
authors: Alireza Kabgani, Moslem Zamani, Masoud Ahookhosh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies difference-of-convex (DC) optimization problems through smoothing descent techniques. In particular, we introduce the difference of high-order Moreau envelopes (HOME-DC) and establish its fundamental and differential properties. Approximating the underlying proximal points, we generate an inexact first-order oracle for HOME-DC and characterize its accuracy guarantees. Building upon this oracle, we propose a class of inexact descent methods for minimizing DC functions and provide a convergence analysis. The proposed framework extends the applicability of envelope-based optimization techniques to a broad class of structured nonconvex problems while accommodating inexact solutions to subproblems. Preliminary numerical experiments on a sparse clustering problem demonstrate the approach's practical potential and support the theoretical findings.
tldr: This paper proposes a new optimization method for difference-of-convex problems using smoothing and inexact oracles, with applications in sparse clustering.
motivation: DC optimization is important in machine learning and signal processing, but existing methods often require exact subproblem solutions or lack convergence guarantees for inexact settings.
method: The authors introduce the difference of high-order Moreau envelopes (HOME-DC), derive its properties, construct an inexact first-order oracle, and propose a class of inexact descent methods with convergence analysis.
result: The proposed framework extends envelope-based techniques to structured nonconvex problems and accommodates inexact subproblem solutions; numerical experiments on sparse clustering show practical potential.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation and practical algorithm for DC optimization with inexact oracles, but its focus is purely on optimization methodology without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Two-stage Semiparametric Inference For Regime-switching Jump Diffusions With Unknown L\'evy Densities
authors: Yuzhong Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study high-frequency semiparametric inference for ergodic regime-switching jump diffusions whose continuous coefficients are parametric and whose regime-wise L\'evy densities are unknown. The motivation is that jumps contaminate increments while their law is itself unknown, making likelihood-based inference circular in switching models. We propose a two-stage procedure. First, small increments are used in a truncated Gaussian quasi-likelihood to estimate the drift and diffusion parameters. Second, large drift-corrected residuals are sorted by regime and smoothed with a kernel, with normalization by empirical regime exposure time, to estimate the L\'evy intensity densities on compact sets away from zero. We establish consistency and mixed-rate asymptotic normality for the quasi-maximum likelihood estimator, and derive \(L^2(B)\)-convergence rates for the exposure-normalized residual density estimator. Simulations for switching Ornstein--Uhlenbeck models illustrate the finite-sample performance of the method.
tldr: This paper develops a two-stage semiparametric inference method for regime-switching jump diffusions with unknown Lévy densities, focusing on high-frequency financial econometrics.
motivation: Jumps contaminate increments while their law is unknown, making likelihood-based inference circular in switching models.
method: First, small increments are used in a truncated Gaussian quasi-likelihood to estimate drift and diffusion parameters. Second, large drift-corrected residuals are sorted by regime and smoothed with a kernel to estimate Lévy intensity densities.
result: Consistency and mixed-rate asymptotic normality for the quasi-maximum likelihood estimator are established, along with L^2 convergence rates for the density estimator.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical solution for inference in regime-switching jump diffusions with unknown jump distributions.

title: Augmenting Airline Networks Using Airside-to-airside Buses To Strengthen System Resilience Under Disruptions
authors: Max Z. Li Micah M. Borrero
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Each year, disruptions in the air transportation network strand millions of passengers and cost airlines billions in revenue. Airline networks prioritize operational and cost efficiency through hub-and-spoke structures that maximize revenue; however, these hubs also act as critical choke points during disruptions. Previous studies have focused on reactionary measures in response to air transportation network disruptions, whereas this work proposes a proactive strategy to improve resilience by reconfiguring the network's topology. Specifically, we consider airside-to-airside bus lines as a low-cost, frequent alternative to short, regional flights, offering service that can circumvent air traffic-related delays. We develop a network construction model that augments the existing air transportation network with these bus lines. The augmented networks are analyzed through an agent-based simulation, where increased resilience is measured in terms of decreased average hourly passenger delays under both nominal and disrupted conditions. Our results demonstrate that converting 10 regional routes from air service to airside-to-airside bus service, for a baseline scenario that is constrained by a $10 million investment budget, can reduce passenger delays by an average of 8% on disrupted days and 6% on nominal days. Furthermore, through a sensitivity analysis, we show that while augmenting the system using these buses decreases operational costs compared to the historic air-only network, continuously expanding bus parameters (i.e., range and investment budget) yields diminishing returns in delay mitigation. Finally, we discuss real-world precedents alongside regulatory and political hurdles to implementation. The proposed framework offers airlines, airports, and regulators a decision-support tool for integrating multimodal strategies into future disruption management policies.
tldr: This paper proposes using airside-to-airside buses to augment airline networks for improved resilience under disruptions.
motivation: Airline disruptions strand passengers and cost revenue; existing reactive measures are insufficient, so a proactive network reconfiguration is needed.
method: A network construction model augments the air transportation network with bus lines; agent-based simulation measures passenger delays under nominal and disrupted conditions.
result: Converting 10 regional routes to bus service reduces passenger delays by 8% on disrupted days and 6% on nominal days, with diminishing returns for further expansion.
conclusion: Airside-to-airside buses offer a low-cost, effective strategy to improve airline network resilience, though regulatory hurdles remain.

title: Peak Sidelobe Suppression In Planar Fluid Antenna Array
authors: Haoyu Liang, Zhentian Zhang, Yuanhui Wu, Jingyuan Xu, Hao Jiang, Zaichen Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FAS) have emerged as a promising technology for next-generation wireless communications, offering inherent reconfigurability and spatial adaptability. A distinctive and practically consequential property of fluid antenna arrays (FAAs) is their geometric diversity: by dynamically activating different subsets of spatially distributed ports across a dense discrete grid, a FAA can reconfigure its effective aperture geometry on demand, thereby unlocking unprecedented spatial degrees of freedom for radiation pattern synthesis. Exploiting such geometric flexibility, this paper investigates peak sidelobe level (PSLL) minimization in sparse planar FAAs through enhanced heuristic optimization. Specifically, an improved genetic algorithm (IGA) is proposed to determine the optimal port activation pattern that minimizes the PSLL under strict sparsity constraints. The proposed IGA incorporates tournament selection, adaptive operator probabilities, a hybrid crossover scheme, multi-point mutation, and an elite-pool preservation strategy to improve both convergence speed and solution quality. Simulation results demonstrate that the IGA significantly outperforms the canonical GA (CGA) in convergence behavior and final PSLL performance, achieving a 4.45 dB reduction in sidelobe levels while maintaining a comparable mainlobe width.
tldr: This paper proposes an improved genetic algorithm to minimize peak sidelobe level in planar fluid antenna arrays for wireless communications.
motivation: Fluid antenna arrays offer geometric diversity that can be exploited for radiation pattern synthesis, but minimizing sidelobe levels under sparsity constraints is challenging.
method: An improved genetic algorithm (IGA) with tournament selection, adaptive operator probabilities, hybrid crossover, multi-point mutation, and elite-pool preservation is used to determine optimal port activation patterns.
result: The IGA achieves a 4.45 dB reduction in peak sidelobe level compared to a canonical genetic algorithm while maintaining comparable mainlobe width.
conclusion: The proposed IGA effectively suppresses sidelobes in sparse planar fluid antenna arrays, demonstrating the potential of geometric diversity for antenna design.

title: A Consistent-splitting Generalized Scalar Auxiliary Variable Scheme For The Perturbed Boussinesq System
authors: M Nader Alhomsi, Jiahong Wu, Xiaoming Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose and analyze a second-order consistent-splitting scheme, based on the generalized scalar auxiliary variable (GSAV) approach, for the two-dimensional perturbed Boussinesq system. The system is obtained by subtracting a stable, linearly stratified hydrostatic equilibrium from the standard Boussinesq system. The time discretization extends the consistent-splitting generalized BDF2 framework of Huang and Shen [17] for the Navier-Stokes equations, treating the nonlinear convection and advection together with the linear buoyancy and stratification couplings explicitly, so that each time step reduces to a small number of decoupled linear systems. We prove an unconditional weak stability theorem for the GSAV scheme and derive optimal second-order error estimates for the velocity, pressure, and temperature. A careful tracing reveals that the error constant depends on the inverse viscosity and inverse thermal diffusivity through a quadruply-nested exponential, so the scheme is not robust as either tends to zero. Numerical experiments confirm the second-order convergence and reproduce the expected internal-wave dynamics and exponential relaxation toward hydrostatic balance in a long-time stratified-flow simulation.
tldr: This paper proposes a numerical scheme for the perturbed Boussinesq system, a fluid dynamics model, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To develop a stable and accurate numerical method for simulating stratified fluid flows, which is a classical fluid dynamics problem.
method: A second-order consistent-splitting generalized scalar auxiliary variable (GSAV) scheme is introduced, extending previous work on Navier-Stokes equations.
result: Unconditional weak stability and optimal second-order error estimates are proved, but the error constant depends exponentially on inverse viscosity and thermal diffusivity.
conclusion: The scheme is effective for stratified flow simulations but not robust for vanishing viscosity or diffusivity.

title: Exclusion Of Infinite Spin For N-body Problem In $\mathbb{R}^d$
authors: Lei Zhao Xiang Yu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that there is no infinite spin at total collisions for [MATH]-homogeneous N-body problem in higher dimensional Euclidean space [MATH], in which [MATH] ([MATH] the Newtonian case), provided the limiting normalized central configuration is isolated and is of dimension d or d - 1. In the Newtonian case [MATH], this extends the work of Moeckel-Montgomery to [MATH] and in the d = 3 case offers a different approach as compared to the current preprint of Pinzari-Zgliczynski.
tldr: This paper proves the absence of infinite spin at total collisions for the N-body problem in higher dimensions under certain conditions.
motivation: To extend previous results on infinite spin in celestial mechanics to higher dimensions and more general homogeneous potentials.
method: The authors use analytical and geometric methods to analyze the behavior of the N-body system near total collisions, assuming the limiting normalized central configuration is isolated and of dimension d or d-1.
result: They show that infinite spin does not occur at total collisions for the given class of homogeneous N-body problems.
conclusion: The result generalizes earlier work by Moeckel-Montgomery and provides a new approach for the Newtonian case in three dimensions.

title: Higher-order Exponential Runge-Kutta Galerkin Finite Element Method For Semilinear Parabolic Problems With Nonsmooth Data
authors: Shuo Yang, Runjie Zhang, Zhe Yu, Jinwei Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a rigorous numerical analysis framework for a class of semilinear parabolic problems with nonsmooth initial data. We employ a linear Galerkin finite element method for spatial discretization coupled with a high-order explicit exponential Runge-Kutta (EERK) temporal integration scheme. In contrast to conventional smooth error analysis, the nonsmooth case lacks a priori estimates for the higher-order derivatives of both the nonlinear term and the exact solution. By combining analytic semigroup techniques with fractional power space theory, we establish rigorous bounds for these derivatives. Finally, our analysis proves that the [MATH]th-order EERK method achieves a convergence rate of [MATH], where [MATH] characterizes the initial data regularity and [MATH] quantifies the boundedness of the nonlinearity's first Fr\'echet derivative. Numerical experiments confirm the sharpness of these estimates.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical analysis framework for semilinear parabolic problems with nonsmooth initial data using exponential Runge-Kutta methods and finite elements.
motivation: Semilinear parabolic problems with nonsmooth initial data are challenging due to lack of a priori estimates for higher-order derivatives; rigorous error bounds are needed.
method: Combines linear Galerkin finite element spatial discretization with high-order explicit exponential Runge-Kutta temporal integration, using analytic semigroup and fractional power space theory.
result: Proves that the m-th order EERK method achieves convergence rate O(h^{r+1} + k^m) with explicit dependence on initial data regularity and nonlinearity boundedness.
conclusion: The proposed method yields sharp convergence rates confirmed by numerical experiments, extending exponential integrator analysis to nonsmooth data.

title: Order Isomorphisms Between Positive Cones Of $c_0(x)$
authors: Natsumi Shibata, Izuho Matsuzaki, Takeshi Miura
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and [MATH] be locally compact Hausdorff spaces. We study order isomorphisms \[ T:C_0^+(X)\to C_0^+(Y), \] where [MATH] denotes the Banach space of all real-valued continuous functions on [MATH] vanishing at infinity, and \[ C_0^+(X)=\{f\in C_0(X):f\ge0\} \] is its positive cone. We assume that [MATH] is positive homogeneous. That is, \[ T(rf)=rT(f) \qquad (r>0,\,f\in C_0^+(X)). \] Under this assumption, we prove that [MATH] is represented as a weighted composition operator induced by a homeomorphism from [MATH] onto [MATH] and a bounded continuous weight function. Moreover, we show that [MATH] extends uniquely to a linear order isomorphism between [MATH] and [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies order isomorphisms between positive cones of continuous function spaces vanishing at infinity, proving they are weighted composition operators.
motivation: To characterize the structure of order isomorphisms between positive cones of C0(X) spaces under positive homogeneity.
method: Using functional analysis and topological arguments, the authors show that any positive homogeneous order isomorphism is a weighted composition operator induced by a homeomorphism and a bounded continuous weight function.
result: The isomorphism extends uniquely to a linear order isomorphism between the full C0 spaces.
conclusion: The result provides a complete classification of such order isomorphisms.

title: Domain-Decomposed Randomized Neural Networks For Partial Differential Equations In Unbounded Domains
authors: Haixin Wang, Haoning Dang, Fei Wang, Shimin Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial differential equations on unbounded domains are challenging because the exterior region must be represented without excessive truncation error. Truncation-based methods often require problem-dependent artificial boundary conditions, while global spectral bases may be inefficient for localized structures, irregular geometries, or solutions with different near-field and far-field behaviors. We propose a domain-decomposed randomized neural network framework for such problems. Different randomized subnetworks are assigned to different spatial regimes: a near-field subnetwork captures local and geometric features, whereas a far-field subnetwork represents exterior decay. The subnetworks are coupled by boundary and interface conditions, and only the output-layer coefficients are solved from linear least-squares systems arising from Petrov--Galerkin or collocation formulations. We develop a Petrov--Galerkin method for semi-unbounded elliptic problems and a collocation method for fully unbounded, perforated, and time-dependent problems. A conditional bounded-parameter approximation result is proved in a broken Sobolev norm, together with an error decomposition covering approximation, empirical-consistency/quadrature, and least-squares optimization errors. Numerical experiments for Poisson and time-dependent Schr\"odinger equations demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.
tldr: This paper proposes a domain-decomposed randomized neural network framework for solving partial differential equations on unbounded domains.
motivation: Solving PDEs on unbounded domains is challenging due to truncation errors and the need for problem-dependent boundary conditions; existing methods are inefficient for localized structures or solutions with different near-field and far-field behaviors.
method: The framework assigns different randomized subnetworks to near-field and far-field regimes, couples them via boundary and interface conditions, and solves for output-layer coefficients using linear least-squares from Petrov-Galerkin or collocation formulations.
result: A conditional bounded-parameter approximation result is proved in a broken Sobolev norm, with an error decomposition covering approximation, empirical-consistency/quadrature, and least-squares optimization errors. Numerical experiments for Poisson and time-dependent Schrödinger equations demonstrate accuracy and flexibility.
conclusion: The proposed method offers an accurate and flexible approach for solving PDEs on unbounded domains without requiring artificial boundary conditions.

title: Bilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund Operators On Vilenkin Groups
authors: Adil Shafi Wani, Qaiser Jahan, Salman Ashraf
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study bilinear Calder\'on--Zygmund operators on a Vilenkin group [MATH]. As a preliminary step, we establish a Grafakos--Torres-type endpoint weak-type result in our setting. Furthermore, we prove that such operators extend to bounded bilinear mappings from [MATH] into [MATH] under the natural condition [MATH] We then obtain a corresponding boundedness result in Morrey spaces, showing that these operators extend to bounded bilinear mappings from [MATH] into [MATH] under suitable assumptions. These results generalize the classical bilinear estimates to the setting of Vilenkin groups.
tldr: This paper studies bilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators on Vilenkin groups, establishing boundedness results in Lebesgue and Morrey spaces.
motivation: To extend classical bilinear harmonic analysis results to the setting of Vilenkin groups, which are a class of locally compact abelian groups with applications in signal processing and number theory.
method: The authors prove a Grafakos-Torres-type endpoint weak-type result and then use interpolation and Fourier analysis on Vilenkin groups to obtain boundedness in Lebesgue and Morrey spaces.
result: The bilinear Calderón-Zygmund operators extend to bounded bilinear mappings from L^{p1} × L^{p2} into L^p under the natural condition 1/p = 1/p1 + 1/p2, and similarly in Morrey spaces.
conclusion: The results generalize classical bilinear estimates to Vilenkin groups, contributing to harmonic analysis on non-abelian or non-Euclidean settings.

title: A Spectral Solver For Acoustic Scattering By Multiple Quasi-Axisymmetric Structures
authors: Yuxin Li Jun Lai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Acoustic scattering arises in a wide range of applications, including medical imaging, geophysical exploration, acoustic metamaterials, etc. In this paper, we develop a fast and highly accurate algorithm for acoustic scattering by multiple quasi-axisymmetric objects, whose axis of rotation is an arbitrary curve. The method is based on a Nystr\"om discretization that combines Gauss-Legendre quadrature with the trapezoidal rule. To treat the singular integrals that occur when target points are close to or coincide with source points, we reformulate them as evaluations of the modal Green's function and its derivatives, which are computed efficiently using the fast Fourier transform and convolution. The multiple scattering solver is then constructed by coupling the single scatterer discretizations through inter-body boundary integral interactions. We also present a convergence analysis for scattering problems with smooth geometries. Numerical examples demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method for solving multiple scattering problems involving up to 1000 quasi-axisymmetric structures.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical algorithm for acoustic scattering by multiple quasi-axisymmetric structures, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Acoustic scattering is important in applications like medical imaging and geophysics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The method uses Nyström discretization with Gauss-Legendre quadrature and trapezoidal rule, and handles singular integrals via modal Green's function and FFT.
result: Numerical examples show efficiency and accuracy for up to 1000 scatterers.
conclusion: The algorithm is effective for classical acoustic scattering but irrelevant to the user's research interests.

title: Joint Planning And Scheduling Of Modular Vehicles For Passenger-Freight Integration
authors: Wanru Chen, Jiaming Wu, Bal\'azs Kulcs\'ar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a modular vehicle system for passenger-freight integration along a bidirectional transit corridor. The system uses homogeneous units that can be coupled into vehicles and assigned to either passenger or freight service. Freight is carried by dedicated units, with loading and unloading coordinated with docking and undocking and separated from passenger boarding and alighting. To better respond to uncertain passenger demand and integrate freight transport, vehicles can be reconfigured at intermediate stations, where they can also depart and terminate. We jointly optimize departure-specific service routes, timetables, vehicle compositions, unit schedules, and passenger-freight demand assignments, with unit reuse constrained by explicit docking and undocking times. These decisions are modeled on a space-time-state network and formulated as a stochastic mixed-integer program that minimizes unit deployment costs, passenger waiting costs, and penalties for unmet freight demand. Passenger demand uncertainty is addressed using linearized chance constraints. To solve the problem, we develop an exact Benders decomposition algorithm with valid inequalities and a warm-start strategy, together with a tailored decomposition-based heuristic for larger instances. Computational experiments on instances generated from representative transit corridors in Gothenburg demonstrate the effectiveness of the Benders algorithm for small- and medium-sized instances and the scalability of the heuristic for larger problems. Sensitivity analyses highlight the value of accounting for passenger demand uncertainty and the effects of temporal overlap between passenger and freight demand. Comparisons with benchmark transit systems further demonstrate the operational advantages of the proposed modular integrated system.
tldr: This paper proposes a modular vehicle system for integrating passenger and freight transport along a transit corridor, using optimization and Benders decomposition.
motivation: To improve urban transit efficiency by jointly planning passenger and freight services using modular vehicles that can be reconfigured at stations.
method: A stochastic mixed-integer program on a space-time-state network with linearized chance constraints for demand uncertainty, solved via exact Benders decomposition with valid inequalities and a heuristic for larger instances.
result: Computational experiments on Gothenburg transit corridors show the Benders algorithm works for small/medium instances and the heuristic scales well; sensitivity analyses highlight benefits of accounting for demand uncertainty.
conclusion: The proposed modular integrated system offers operational advantages over benchmark transit systems, demonstrating the value of joint passenger-freight planning with vehicle reconfiguration.

title: Exponential Rate Of Convergence Of Relative Value Iteration Algorithms For Ergodic Controls Of Diffusions
authors: Guodong Pang Sumith Reddy Anugu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the rate of convergence of the relative value iteration (RVI) algorithms for diffusions in [MATH] under both the conventional ergodic cost (CEC) and ergodic risk-sensitive cost (ERSC) criteria, and under the uniform exponential stability condition. The existing RVI algorithms for the CEC and ERSC problems solve the associated initial value Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman type equations whose solutions are shown to converge asymptotically to the corresponding optimal values. However, the rates of convergence for such algorithms have remained open. This paper proposes discrete-time implementations for the RVI algorithms based on slight modifications of the associated PDEs, and proves that the rates of convergence of these RVI algorithms are exponential under a weighted sup-norm. These implementations have discrete-time iterates that can be explicitly expressed as recursive systems. The difference between these iterates and the desired value function in the CEC case can then be expressed in terms of the associated Markov kernels. Similarly, this can be done for the logarithms of the corresponding iterates and desired value function in the ERSC case in terms of the associated Markov kernels for the extended diffusion. As a result, we are able to prove the desirable contraction properties in order to establish the exponential rate of convergence by making use of a weighted semi-norm in which Markov kernel acts a contraction.
tldr: This paper proves exponential convergence rates for relative value iteration algorithms in ergodic control of diffusions, a topic in stochastic control theory.
motivation: The rate of convergence for RVI algorithms in ergodic control of diffusions was an open problem; establishing it is crucial for algorithm efficiency.
method: The authors propose discrete-time implementations of RVI algorithms based on modified PDEs and analyze contraction properties using weighted sup-norms and Markov kernels.
result: They prove that the RVI algorithms converge exponentially under a weighted sup-norm for both conventional ergodic cost and ergodic risk-sensitive cost criteria.
conclusion: The exponential convergence rate is established, filling a theoretical gap in the analysis of RVI algorithms for diffusions.

title: Ilpu: Iterative Laplace-Based Phase Unwrapping Via Bi-Level Optimization
authors: Michael Fedders, Jakob Schattenfroh, Yanglei Wu, Noah Jaitner, Tom Meyer, Jakob Jordan, Jing Guo, Ingolf Sack, Hossein S. Aghamiry
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase unwrapping is an essential preprocessing step for phase-based MRI applications, including susceptibility mapping, field mapping, thermometry, and MR elastography. We present Iterative Laplace-Based Phase Unwrapping (ILPU), a bi-level optimization algorithm. In this method, a lower-level solver recovers a continuous phase increment from an incremental Poisson equation using the discrete cosine transform (DCT), while an upper-level solver refines an integer offset map through quality-guided spatial regularization and a restricted local search. This coupling enables robust unwrapping in low-SNR regions through adaptive smoothness penalties and quality-weighted regularization. We evaluated ILPU on 2D and 3D brain MRI phase images against manually unwrapped reference data, using standard Laplace unwrapping, Flynn, and SEGUE as comparison methods. In 2D, ILPU achieves accuracy comparable to SEGUE. In 3D, ILPU attains a relative error of 2.12% compared with 67.59% for SEGUE and 81.02% for Laplace, demonstrating a clear advantage in volumetric unwrapping. The algorithm has O(N log N) complexity per iteration through DCT-based Laplacian estimation and is numerically faster than both Flynn and SEGUE while preserving superior accuracy. These results indicate that the bi-level optimization framework provides a robust and computationally efficient solution for phase unwrapping in MRI.
tldr: This paper presents a bi-level optimization algorithm for phase unwrapping in MRI, which is a classical image processing problem with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Phase unwrapping is essential for MRI applications like susceptibility mapping and elastography, but existing methods struggle with low-SNR regions and volumetric data.
method: ILPU uses a lower-level solver to recover a continuous phase increment via DCT-based Poisson equation and an upper-level solver to refine integer offsets through quality-guided regularization and local search.
result: ILPU achieves 2.12% relative error in 3D brain MRI compared to 67.59% for SEGUE and 81.02% for Laplace, with O(N log N) complexity.
conclusion: The bi-level optimization framework provides a robust and efficient solution for phase unwrapping in MRI.

title: An Error Analysis Of Discrete Kirchhoff Elements
authors: Ngoc Tien Tran Dietmar Gallistl
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Discrete Kirchhoff Triangle (DKT) method for the biharmonic equation is analyzed in the discrete energy norm. The error is bounded by the best approximation of the Hessian by piecewise constants and the oscillation of the right-hand side, without additional regularity assumptions on the exact solution. This result implies first-order convergence of the classical DKT element and the analysis yields a canonical extension to three space dimensions with the same approximation properties. Residual-based a posteriori error estimates are derived. The analysis is formulated within a general framework for low-order nonconforming methods, which also applies to various classical elements and yields best-approximation results by constants. It is furthermore shown how known stable pairs for the planar Stokes system have discrete stream functions in discrete Kirchhoff spaces. This yields variants of the known schemes with positive definite formulations and pressure-robust error bounds.
tldr: This paper presents an error analysis of Discrete Kirchhoff Triangle (DKT) elements for the biharmonic equation, focusing on numerical analysis and finite element methods.
motivation: The paper aims to provide a rigorous error analysis for DKT elements without additional regularity assumptions, and to extend the framework to 3D and a posteriori error estimates.
method: The analysis uses a general framework for low-order nonconforming methods, bounding the error by best approximation of the Hessian by piecewise constants and oscillation of the right-hand side.
result: First-order convergence is proved for the classical DKT element, and the analysis extends canonically to three dimensions with the same approximation properties.
conclusion: The work provides a unified analysis for several classical nonconforming elements and shows connections to stable pairs for the Stokes system.

title: Antenna Orientation Optimization For Rotatable Antenna-Enabled Isac Systems
authors: Qingjie Wu, Beixiong Zheng, Guangchi Zhang, Robert Schober
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rotatable antenna (RA) has emerged as a promising technology to improve both communication and sensing performance in future wireless networks. In this paper, we deploy an RA array at the base station (BS) to improve the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) performance by exploiting the additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) introduced by antenna rotation. To enhance the sensing performance over an extended region containing a potential target while meeting the communication requirements of multiple users, we aim to maximize the minimum echo signal power within the sensing region, subject to required minimum communication rates of the users. For the special case of a single user and a point target, we show that the optimal orientation of all RAs is identical when both the communication user and the sensing target are located in the far-field region, and then derive a closed-form solution for the optimal RA pointing vector. For the general multi-user and extended-target case, we propose an alternating optimization (AO) algorithm that alternately optimizes the transmit beamforming for communication, the covariance matrix of the probing signal, and the pointing vectors of the RAs in an iterative manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed RA-enabled ISAC system can significantly outperform various benchmark schemes, including systems with array-wise rotation optimization and fixed antenna orientation.
tldr: This paper optimizes antenna orientation in rotatable antenna-enabled integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems to improve sensing performance while meeting communication rate constraints.
motivation: Rotatable antennas can provide additional spatial degrees of freedom to enhance both communication and sensing performance in future wireless networks.
method: The authors formulate an optimization problem to maximize the minimum echo signal power within a sensing region subject to communication rate constraints, and propose an alternating optimization algorithm to jointly optimize transmit beamforming, covariance matrix, and antenna pointing vectors.
result: Simulation results show that the proposed RA-enabled ISAC system significantly outperforms benchmark schemes with fixed antenna orientation or array-wise rotation optimization.
conclusion: Optimizing antenna orientation in ISAC systems can substantially improve sensing coverage while maintaining communication quality.

title: Generalized Laura-Andoyer Equations And The Enumeration Of Some Symmetrical Classes Of Dziobek Configurations
authors: Ya-Lun Tsai Thiago Dias
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the symmetrical Dziobek configurations where, in [MATH], there are [MATH] bodies with unit masses at the vertices of a regular [MATH]-dimensional simplex of unit edge length and two more bodies with nonzero masses [MATH] are on the line passing through the center of the simplex and being orthogonal to it. In the case of logarithmic potential, the finiteness is proved for all [MATH], and we obtain the bifurcation surface in the [MATH]-space through Gr\"obner basis computation. Using cylindrical algebraic decompositions, we find [MATH] sample points in the complement of the bifurcation surface. We propose a method to reduce the number to only [MATH]. By Hermite's root counting theorem, we find that, generically, there can be [MATH] or [MATH] concave, [MATH] or [MATH] convex, and in totality, [MATH] or [MATH] such configurations for all dimensions [MATH]. For positive [MATH] and [MATH], generically, there is a unique convex configuration, while the number of concave ones can be [MATH] or [MATH]. All possible combinations for the numbers described above are realized when [MATH]. We obtain a set of generalized Laura-Andoyer equations equivalent to the central configurations equations for all fixed number of bodies [MATH] and configuration dimension [MATH]. For homogeneous force law with exponent [MATH], we use the action of permutation group [MATH] in the Laura-Andoyer equations to reduce the equivalent [MATH] Laura-Andoyer equations to only two generalized polynomial algebraic equations for the studied class of symmetric configurations with two variables representing the positions of the two bodies not at the vertices of the simplex in four parameters [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies symmetrical Dziobek configurations in celestial mechanics, deriving generalized Laura-Andoyer equations and enumerating concave/convex configurations.
motivation: To understand the finiteness and classification of symmetrical central configurations in the n-body problem, specifically Dziobek configurations with a regular simplex and two additional bodies.
method: Uses Gröbner basis computation, cylindrical algebraic decomposition, and Hermite's root counting theorem to analyze algebraic equations derived from the Laura-Andoyer equations.
result: Proves finiteness for all dimensions, finds bifurcation surfaces, and determines generic numbers of concave and convex configurations for various parameter ranges.
conclusion: The work provides a complete enumeration and algebraic characterization of a class of symmetrical Dziobek configurations, extending classical results in celestial mechanics.

title: Understanding And Evaluating Claw-like Agent Security Through A Computer-Systems Lens
authors: Peizhi Niu, Wenjie Qu, Shangding Gu, Tianneng Shi, Yuankai Li, Ahmad Tawaha, Hend Alzahrani, Vincent Siu, Boyi Li, Chenguang Wang, Jiaheng Zhang, Basel Alomair, Ming Jin, Muhao Chen, Chi Wang, Costas Spanos, Dawn Song
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Claw-like AI agents (e.g., OpenClaw) are always-on processes with persistent access to credentials, files, tools, and external services. They take on system-level responsibilities -- installing packages, maintaining state, scheduling subtasks, and mediating I/O -- making security failures far more severe than in other agents. Yet existing benchmarks focus on model responses and tool calls, leaving cross-component failure modes largely unmeasured. We adopt a computer-system analogy: treating a Claw-like agent as an agentic computer system whose gateway runtime plays an OS-like mediation role, whose Skills resemble user-installed applications, and whose Plugins resemble loadable extensions with runtime privileges. Each component has a classical counterpart whose protection mechanisms -- refined over decades of cybersecurity research -- are absent on the agent side. From this perspective, we develop SafeClawArena, a benchmark of 406 adversarial tasks across four attack surfaces (Skill Supply-Chain Integrity, Persistent State Exploitation, Cross-Boundary Data Flow, and Indirect Prompt Injection), executed in containerized replicas of real agent platforms with canary-marked credentials and evaluated via automated taint tracking across nine output channels. We evaluate three platforms (OpenClaw, NemoClaw, SeClaw) and five frontier LLMs. The highest attack success rate reaches 70%; malicious Plugins succeed in 100% of cases regardless of the LLM. SeClaw cuts GPT-5.4's attack success rate from 70% to 22%, partly through utility-security tradeoffs rather than active defenses, while Claude-Opus-4.6 already sits near a 22% floor on every platform. These results expose the inadequacy of current defenses and suggest directions for future hardening. Code and data: [URL].
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in claw-like AI agents through a computer-systems analogy, focusing on cross-component failure modes.
motivation: Existing benchmarks for AI agent security overlook cross-component failures that can lead to severe security breaches.
method: The authors develop SafeClawArena, a benchmark with 406 adversarial tasks across four attack surfaces, and evaluate three agent platforms and five LLMs using automated taint tracking.
result: The highest attack success rate reaches 70%; malicious Plugins succeed in 100% of cases regardless of the LLM. SeClaw reduces GPT-5.4's attack success rate from 70% to 22%.
conclusion: Current defenses are inadequate, and the paper suggests directions for future hardening of claw-like agents.

title: Optimal Auctions For Constrained Buyers
authors: Batya Berzack, Rotem Oshman, Inbal Talgam-Cohen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multi-unit multi-buyer auctions, where buyers are subject to constraints that affect their bidding strategy. These may take the form of (e.g., no-overbidding, in cases where bids are partially verifiable), or of (e.g., in the case of auctions that unfold over time, an inability to go into debt even temporarily). The constraints fundamentally redefine the design space: the revelation principle, the envelope theorem, and Myerson's lemma do not apply in this constrained setting. Consequently, the space of implementable mechanisms expands significantly, admitting auctions that are incentive compatible with respect to the constrained buyers' utility, but would not be incentive compatible in the classical sense. In this paper we focus on monotone constraints where it is not the buyers' total budget that is restricted, but rather the manner in which they can bid or spend their budget. Our results show a separation between objectives (e.g., revenue, welfare, or any linear combination of the two) and objectives (e.g., consumer surplus). For revenue-aligned objectives, we rely on measure-theoretic tools to establish a unified theory parallel to Myerson, showing that despite the expanded design space, Myerson-style auctions remain optimal. For consumer-aligned objectives, the picture is different: we show that the seller can leverage the buyers' strategic limitations to strictly outperform classically incentive compatible mechanisms. We design the optimal deterministic auction for a wide class of instances, focusing in particular on buyers who cannot tolerate temporary debt. Overall, our work provides theoretical underpinnings for this area and shows that a rigorous and systematic approach can reveal general insights regarding optimal auction design.
tldr: This paper studies optimal auction design under buyer constraints like no-overbidding or no-debt, using measure-theoretic tools to characterize optimal mechanisms.
motivation: Classical auction theory assumes unconstrained buyers, but real-world constraints (e.g., no-overbidding, no-debt) break standard tools like the revelation principle. The authors aim to develop a theory for optimal auctions under such constraints.
method: The paper focuses on monotone constraints that restrict how buyers can bid or spend, and uses measure-theoretic tools to derive optimal mechanisms for revenue-aligned objectives, while for consumer-aligned objectives they design optimal deterministic auctions.
result: For revenue-aligned objectives, Myerson-style auctions remain optimal despite the expanded design space. For consumer-aligned objectives, the seller can outperform classically incentive-compatible mechanisms by leveraging buyer constraints.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous theoretical foundation for optimal auction design under buyer constraints, showing that systematic analysis yields general insights.

title: Security--Fidelity Tradeoffs: The Hidden Cost Of Prompt Injection Defense
authors: Mitchell Hermon, Rahul Gupta, Weitong Ruan, Ekraam Sabir, Haohan Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify a security-fidelity tradeoff in defending LLMs against indirect prompt injection: defenses resist injected instructions largely by suppressing untrusted text, which corrupts tasks that must preserve it, such as translation and document editing. Attack-success metrics cannot see this, because a model that ignores an injection and one that faithfully processes it as data score identically. We introduce SecFid, a benchmark built so that executing an injection, processing it as data, and ignoring it produce distinguishable outputs. This makes fidelity measurable and exposes a frontier: across 1,168 examples and 48 configurations, no model or defense achieves both objectives. The highest-fidelity model reaches 96.5% fidelity at 47.8% security, while the most secure defenses invert this, at 99.3% security but only 71.0%-73.9% fidelity. Even defenses with identical security differ in how they earn it: some repair hijacks into faithful processing, others simply suppress benign content. A decision-theoretic analysis shows why no fixed choice can be right everywhere: the correct behavior is not a property of the defense but of the deployment, set by its relative cost of a hijack versus a dropped span. Security alone therefore measures only half of robustness, and reporting it without fidelity hides the price at which it was bought.
tldr: This paper identifies a security-fidelity tradeoff in defending LLMs against indirect prompt injection, showing that defenses that suppress untrusted text harm tasks requiring faithful text preservation.
motivation: Current attack-success metrics fail to capture fidelity loss when defenses suppress benign content, hiding the true cost of security.
method: The authors introduce SecFid, a benchmark that distinguishes between executing an injection, processing it as data, and ignoring it, enabling measurement of both security and fidelity across 1,168 examples and 48 configurations.
result: No model or defense achieves both high security and high fidelity; the highest-fidelity model reaches 96.5% fidelity at 47.8% security, while the most secure defenses achieve 99.3% security but only 71.0%-73.9% fidelity.
conclusion: Security alone is insufficient; reporting fidelity is necessary to understand the true robustness of defenses, and the optimal behavior depends on deployment-specific costs.

title: AI-Generated PowerShell Malware: An Experimental Framework And Dataset
authors: Luciano Pianese, Vittorio Orbinato, Pietro Liguori, Roberto Natella
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI has emerged as a significant cybersecurity threat, with several recent attack campaigns leveraging LLMs to generate code for malicious purposes via scripting languages such as PowerShell. Consequently, for cybersecurity analysts, it is imperative to investigate the offensive capabilities of AI code generators. In this paper, we propose an experimental framework to assess LLM-generated PowerShell malware, which comprises a novel sandbox approach for dynamic analysis of AI-generated malware. Furthermore, we present a novel, manually curated dataset of real-world PowerShell malware, annotated in natural language to assist the training and evaluation of LLMs. Finally, this study evaluates permissive, open-weight LLMs adapted to PowerShell malware generation. Our results reveal a high degree of similarity between real malware and LLM-generated ones in terms of triggered OS malicious events, with a median Jaccard index of 84.5% and 48.4% of instances achieving complete overlap.
tldr: This paper presents an experimental framework and dataset for analyzing AI-generated PowerShell malware, focusing on cybersecurity threats from LLMs.
motivation: Generative AI poses a cybersecurity threat as LLMs can generate malicious code; analysts need tools to assess offensive capabilities of AI code generators.
method: The authors propose a sandbox approach for dynamic analysis of AI-generated PowerShell malware and create a manually curated dataset of real-world PowerShell malware annotated in natural language.
result: LLM-generated malware shows high similarity to real malware in triggered OS events, with median Jaccard index of 84.5% and 48.4% instances achieving complete overlap.
conclusion: The framework and dataset enable evaluation of LLM-generated malware, highlighting the need for defenses against AI-generated cyber threats.

title: Automated Reasoning With Nested Datatypes
authors: Tomer Hakak, Yoni Zohar, Andrew Reynolds, Clark Barrett, Cesare Tinelli
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a theory of nested datatypes. The theory is obtained by restricting the naive combination of datatypes and arrays, so as to prevent non-standard models from emerging. A decision procedure for the theory is given and proven correct. Finally, we describe an implementation of the procedure, as well as an evaluation over both real-world and crafted benchmarks.
tldr: This paper introduces a theory of nested datatypes and a decision procedure for it, with an implementation and evaluation.
motivation: The naive combination of datatypes and arrays leads to non-standard models; a restricted theory is needed to avoid this.
method: A theory of nested datatypes is defined by restricting the combination of datatypes and arrays, and a decision procedure is proven correct.
result: The decision procedure is implemented and evaluated on real-world and crafted benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed theory and decision procedure effectively handle nested datatypes without non-standard models.

title: Curvature-Guided Module Localization For Low-Rank Detoxification Of Backdoored Large Language Models
authors: Arash Raftari, Mehrdad Mahdavi, Nathan Blackthorn, Andrew Arash Mahyari
abstract: ArXiv:2606.30899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to large language models (LLMs) by causing otherwise benign systems to produce attacker-specified malicious behavior when a hidden trigger is present. In this work, we study post hoc detoxification of backdoored LLMs in a practical setting where the defender has access to the poisoned model but does not wish to retrain the full network from scratch. We propose a mechanistically guided weight-space repair framework that first localizes modules involved in propagating trigger-induced behavior using activation patching and Fisher/K-FAC curvature analysis, and then applies targeted low-rank repair to only the most influential modules. We evaluate the method on poisoned variants of with triggers inserted at the beginning, middle, and end of otherwise benign prompts. Results show that the proposed approach substantially suppresses trigger-conditioned malicious responses while preserving benign model behavior. These findings suggest that backdoor removal in LLMs can be formulated as a localized structural repair problem rather than only a broad behavioral alignment problem.
tldr: This paper proposes a curvature-guided module localization method for low-rank detoxification of backdoored large language models.
motivation: Backdoor attacks pose a serious threat to LLMs, and existing detoxification methods often require full retraining or are not targeted.
method: The method uses activation patching and Fisher/K-FAC curvature analysis to localize modules involved in trigger-induced behavior, then applies targeted low-rank repair to those modules.
result: The approach substantially suppresses trigger-conditioned malicious responses while preserving benign model behavior.
conclusion: Backdoor removal in LLMs can be formulated as a localized structural repair problem rather than only a broad behavioral alignment problem.

title: Secure-CHG: A Comprehensive Framework For Robust And Fair Federated Learning Via Hybrid Defense And Contribution-Aware Trust
authors: Guanming Che, Qiang Wang, Jian Xu, Fucai Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is highly susceptible to stealthy backdoor attacks, which aim to force a model into predicting an attacker-chosen target class for inputs containing a specific trigger. However, existing statistical defenses primarily focus on the early stages of model convergence. In this paper, we identify a fundamental vulnerability termed ``Late-stage Failure.'' We demonstrate that as the global model converges, decaying gradient norms render malicious and benign updates morphologically indistinguishable. This vanishing statistical variance effectively blinds traditional defenses, enabling adaptive adversaries to remain dormant and subsequently hijack the training process. To overcome these constraints, we propose Secure-CHG, a hybrid framework that pivots the defense paradigm from superficial morphological detection toward intrinsic semantic contribution verification. Secure-CHG employs an adaptive defense pipeline: a cascaded statistical filter stabilizes optimization during the early oscillatory phase, while a novel CHG-Shapley mechanism takes over during late-stage convergence. By leveraging sample hardness (i.e., local training loss) to project updates into a composite Hardness-Gradient space, it effectively amplifies adversarial semantic traces, enabling the isolation of stealthy attackers even as gradient norms vanish. Furthermore, we derive a closed-form solution for CHG-Shapley, facilitating low-complexity, retraining-free node valuation and trust-modulated aggregation. Extensive evaluations on CIFAR-10, MedMNIST, and NEU-SDDB demonstrate that Secure-CHG effectively mitigates Late-stage Failure. Specifically, it significantly suppresses advanced backdoor attacks, reducing their attack success rate by 2.3[MATH] and 2.0[MATH] relative to the mainstream Krum and Trimmed Mean baselines, respectively.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated learning defense framework against backdoor attacks, focusing on late-stage convergence vulnerabilities.
motivation: Federated learning is vulnerable to backdoor attacks, and existing defenses fail during late-stage convergence when gradient norms vanish.
method: Secure-CHG uses a cascaded statistical filter for early stages and a CHG-Shapley mechanism for late-stage detection, leveraging sample hardness to amplify adversarial traces.
result: Experiments on CIFAR-10, MedMNIST, and NEU-SDDB show Secure-CHG reduces attack success rate by 2.3× and 2.0× compared to Krum and Trimmed Mean baselines.
conclusion: The hybrid defense effectively mitigates late-stage backdoor attacks in federated learning.

title: Beyond But-for Test: Counterfactual Explanation In Abstract Argumentation Via Actual Causality (Extended Version)
authors: Siyi Liu, Muyun Shao, Beishui Liao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Counterfactual explanation in abstract argumentation calls for an answer to the what-if query: would the topic argument still be accepted if the status of certain other arguments were changed? Existing approaches are limited to the but-for test and fail to accommodate more refined counterfactual conditions. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an intervention-based counterfactual reasoning framework in abstract argumentation. Our approach encodes the acceptance conditions of arguments as equations, then defines an intervention operator that supports (1) changing sets of arguments simultaneously, and (2) fixing witness arguments to their actual labels. Guided by the refined counterfactual condition introduced in the Halpern-Pearl definition, our method goes beyond the but-for test, thereby correctly identifying causes in argumentation structures such as Preemption and Overdetermination. Through comparison, we show that our method surpasses prior methods in both expressiveness and reliability.
tldr: This paper proposes a counterfactual explanation framework in abstract argumentation using actual causality, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Existing counterfactual explanations in abstract argumentation are limited to the but-for test and fail to handle refined conditions like preemption and overdetermination.
method: The authors encode argument acceptance conditions as equations and define an intervention operator that supports changing sets of arguments and fixing witness arguments, guided by the Halpern-Pearl definition of actual causality.
result: The proposed method surpasses prior methods in expressiveness and reliability, correctly identifying causes in argumentation structures such as Preemption and Overdetermination.
conclusion: The intervention-based framework provides a more refined counterfactual reasoning approach for abstract argumentation.

title: Probe Choice Changes Canary-Memorization Verdicts: Three Post-Hoc Disagreement Case Studies In A Text-Dominant LoRA-Tuned Autoregressive Testbed
authors: Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang, Yanhang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We audit a fixed prefix-window mean-NLL memorization probe (K=20) on a Qwen2.5-VL-7B canary testbed and report three post-hoc cases where it disagrees with full-span secret NLL or greedy exact-recall. C3 (false negative, window truncation): damage lands on hex tokens outside K=20; the probe stays flat while hit@1 drops. C4 (false positive, non-secret drift): the probe moves, but approximately 99% sits on non-secret preamble; the secret span and hit@1 are unchanged. C5 (ambiguous in-window drop): the probe falls on an undertrained baseline while full-span hex is positive and hit@1=0. Recommendation: report (i) full-span secret NLL, (ii) a span-localised decomposition, (iii) behavioural exact-recall at k>=4, and (iv) decoy probes before asserting secret-specificity. Evidence is on controlled canaries in one backbone; magnitudes are testbed-specific.
tldr: This paper audits a memorization probe on a vision-language model and finds disagreements with other metrics, but it is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The authors aim to evaluate the reliability of a specific memorization probe in detecting canary memorization in a text-dominant LoRA-tuned autoregressive model.
method: They compare a fixed prefix-window mean-NLL probe with full-span secret NLL and greedy exact-recall on a Qwen2.5-VL-7B canary testbed, analyzing three post-hoc disagreement cases.
result: They identify three cases: false negative due to window truncation, false positive due to non-secret drift, and ambiguous in-window drop, showing that probe choice can change memorization verdicts.
conclusion: They recommend reporting multiple metrics including full-span secret NLL, span-localized decomposition, behavioral exact-recall, and decoy probes before asserting secret-specificity.

title: Securing The Ai Agent: A Unified Framework For Multi-Layer Agent Red Teaming
authors: Yong Yang, Xing Zheng, Huiyu Wu, Huangsheng Cheng, Xiaorong Shi, Jing Guo, Bo Yang, Yi Zhou, Xiangfan Wu, Zonghao Ying
abstract: ArXiv:2606.31227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fast growth of open-source AI infrastructure, from model serving engines and agent platforms to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem and the language models themselves, has outpaced the security tooling available to defend it.
